comment: Agent with two tools: generate_image (image_generation) and upload_image_multipart (http_request in multipart mode targeting httpbin /post). The model must chain: (1) generate, (2) take attachment_id from the response, (3) call upload with body={'files': ['$attachment:<id>'], 'metadata': '...'}. Validates the full LLM tool-calling flow with the new multipart streaming feature.

test_payload.prompt: Generá una imagen de un gato astronauta en la luna y subila al servidor de prueba con metadata 'lunar feline test'.

config.system_message:
You are an agent with two tools: generate_image and upload_image_multipart. Workflow MUST be exactly this:

1. Call generate_image with a detailed visual prompt derived from the user's request.
2. The tool response contains `images[0].attachment_id` (a string like 'abc123.png'). Take that value.
3. Call upload_image_multipart with body = { "files": ["$attachment:<attachment_id>"], "metadata": "<short text from user>" }. The first element of files MUST be the literal string '$attachment:' followed by the attachment_id — for example, if attachment_id is 'abc123.png' then files should be ['$attachment:abc123.png'].
4. After upload returns (status 200 expected), write a 1-2 sentence summary mentioning the attachment_id and that it was uploaded successfully.

Do NOT skip tools. Do NOT describe intentions — execute them.

generate_image.name: generate_image
generate_image.description: Generate a brand-new image from a text prompt using gpt-image-1. Returns { images: [{ attachment_id, url, mime_type, size_bytes, description }], provider, model }. The attachment_id is a stable handle you can pass to other tools via the prefix '$attachment:<attachment_id>'.

prompt.description: Detailed text prompt describing the image to generate.

upload_image_multipart.name: upload_image_multipart
upload_image_multipart.description: Upload one or more generated files to the test server via multipart/form-data. Use AFTER generate_image. The `body` argument must be an object with 'files' (array of strings; each either an https:// URL or '$attachment:<attachment_id>' referencing a previously generated artifact) and 'metadata' (free-text note). Returns { status, body } from the server.

body.description: Multipart form body. Must be a JSON object with two fields: 'files' (array of strings; each either an https URL or '$attachment:<attachment_id>') and 'metadata' (string, short text note).
